correctness.rationale: The determinant identity is exact; irreducibility follows from primitive linearity in the center diagonal. Rank-corank equivalence to the gradient follows from symmetric corank-one adjugates. Schur complement on nonzero leaf diagonals exhausts zero-leaf counts and proves all minimal primes set-theoretically. Radicality and scheme equality follow from Deng--Kretschmer Theorem 1, which directly includes connected-star patterns. All listed primes have height three and distinct generic points; degrees sum to m^2+binom(m,3). Near generic single-leaf components F=a_i F_i-b_i^2P_i gives a split quadratic; near generic triple-leaf components the transverse Hessian is nondegenerate in characteristic not two. The packaged enumerator directly checks small finite cases; it is not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: For every star size, a natural linear section of the symmetric determinant hypersurface has its entire singular support decomposed into exactly m+binom(m,3) irreducible codimension-three components, with their degrees and both generic local analytic types; this explains the geometric multiplicity of a highly structured sparse determinant beyond prior general homological invariants. The exact prime list is useful for resolving singularities and understanding component intersections, not just an arbitrary numerical slice.
